flashcards.back: The smallest particle of an element that keeps its chemical identity: a tiny dense nucleus with electrons in shells around mostly empty space.
The tiny dense centre of the atom, holding the protons and neutrons. Almost all the atom's mass sits here.
A particle in the nucleus with charge +1 and mass 1. The number of protons - the proton number - fixes which element the atom is.
A particle in the nucleus with no charge and mass 1. Neutrons = nucleon number - proton number.
A particle with charge -1 and almost no mass, sitting in fixed shells around the nucleus. A neutral atom has equal electrons and protons.
A fixed energy level around the nucleus where electrons sit. Shells fill in order: shell 1 holds 2, shell 2 holds 8, shell 3 holds 8.
A column of the periodic table. Elements in one group share the same number of outer electrons, so they react in similar ways.
A row of the periodic table. The period number matches the number of electron shells the atoms have.

The slip: The ball-and-stick model is everywhere, so atoms look like tiny solid marbles. The fix: Atoms are mostly empty space: the electrons sit far from a tiny dense nucleus. In class, compare the two pictures side by side: the solid marble, then the shell model with its speck of a nucleus - and ask which one explains why alpha particles mostly passed straight through gold foil.
Atoms are mostly empty space, with electrons in shells around a tiny dense nucleus
flashcards.front: A student draws an atom as a solid ball. What is the best correction?

flashcards.back: 6 protons, 12 - 6 = 6 neutrons and 6 electrons. The six electrons fill the shells two, then four, so the arrangement is 2,4.
flashcards.front: Carbon has proton number 6 and nucleon number 12. State its numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons, and write its electron arrangement.

items.answer: Atoms are mostly empty space, with electrons in shells around a tiny dense nucleus
items.prompt: A student draws an atom as a solid ball. What is the best correction?

items.answer: A tiny dense nucleus with electrons in fixed shells, and mostly empty space between
items.prompt: Which picture of the atom is correct?
An element's atoms have three electron shells, with 6 electrons in the outer shell. In which period and group does it sit?

items.answer: Period 3, because it has three electron shells; group 5, because it has 5 electrons in its outer shell.
items.prompt: An element has electron arrangement 2,8,5. State its period and its group, and explain each answer.
